item.mechanism: Dislocation network formation due to thermal contraction strain during rapid solidification and cooling in SLM acts as a primary strengthening mechanism.
item.system: Equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi HEA additively manufactured by Selective Laser Melting (SLM)
item.operating_conditions: As-built state (rapid solidification and cooling), room temperature to 700 °C compression
item.supporting_observation: Higher dislocation density of 1.88 × 10^14 m^-2 compared to homogenized HEA, attributed to thermal contraction strain of approximately 0–2%.
item.scope_limits: Not stated where this mechanism fails, but the authors note that matrix hardening and grain boundary strengthening contributions decrease significantly at high temperatures due to thermally activated mechanisms.
item.alternatives_considered: Conventional thermomechanical processing routes (casting, rolling, annealing) which result in lower dislocation densities.
quotes: This is a common tendency found in AM-processed materials, and it is known to be caused by thermal contraction strain that occurs during rapid solidification and cooling.
Linear thermal strain ( ∆ ε ) during cooling is approximately 0–2%, and the thermal contraction stress occurring at this stage can form a large number of dislocations.
The SLM-built HEA has a higher dislocation density of 1.88 × 10 14 m −2 as compared to the homogenized HEA.

item.mechanism: Nano-sized Mn2O3 oxides provide Orowan strengthening by pinning dislocations and delaying recrystallization via the Zener drag effect.
item.system: Equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi HEA additively manufactured by Selective Laser Melting (SLM)
item.operating_conditions: Room temperature to 900 °C compression; as-built state with nano-precipitates at cell boundaries
item.supporting_observation: Mn2O3 particles of 27.3 nm size observed at cell boundaries; high volume fraction and small particle diameter increase Zener pinning pressure, delaying recrystallization up to 900 °C.
item.scope_limits: Does not hold for preventing σ-phase formation in general HEAs, as SLM specifically avoids Cr-Mn-based oxides or σ-phases found in other processing methods.
item.alternatives_considered: Cr-Mn-based oxides or σ-phase formation which can hinder mechanical properties; interstitial solute atoms for serration.
quotes: SLM-built HEA did not form a Cr-Mn-based oxide or σ-phase, which can partially hinder the mechanical properties of the alloy, and only Mn 2 O 3 tens of nm in size was identified.
As SLM-built equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi HEA has a high fraction F v and d of 27.3 nm, P Z increases significantly.
Therefore, while P D is identical, the overall pressure for recrystallization decreases as a result of the Zener pinning pressure ( P Z ) caused by Mn 2 O 3.

item.mechanism: Slip and deformation twinning (DT) are the dominant deformation mechanisms at low temperatures (25 °C to 600 °C), contributing to work hardening.
item.system: Equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi HEA additively manufactured by Selective Laser Melting (SLM)
item.supporting_observation: EBSD and ECC images show a large number of deformation twins (θ ≈ 60°) and no dynamic recrystallization; work hardening continues in this range.
item.scope_limits: Does not hold above 700 °C where dynamic recrystallization becomes dominant.
item.alternatives_considered: Dynamic recovery or dynamic recrystallization which occur at higher temperatures.
quotes: Based on the above findings, it was confirmed that the major deformation mechanisms were slip and deformation twinning that occurred from room temperature up to 600 °C.
In EBSD IPF maps at a macro strain of 40%, a large number of deformation twins (DTs, θ ≈ 60°) were observed at room temperature.

In the range of temperatures above 700 °C, the deformed samples had a clear cellular and columnar structure composed of dislocation networks as well as nano-sized oxides, and this confirmed that the slip and partial RX observed in EBSD are the main deformation mechanisms.

item.mechanism: Slip and partial dynamic recrystallization (DRX) are the dominant deformation mechanisms at high temperatures (≥700 °C), causing work softening.
item.system: Equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi HEA additively manufactured by Selective Laser Melting (SLM)
item.supporting_observation: Grains of hundreds of nm to few μm observed at grain boundaries; yield strength drop and work softening occur; substructured and recrystallized regions observed.
item.scope_limits: Full recrystallization does not occur easily up to 900 °C due to Zener drag from oxides and migrated grain boundaries.
item.alternatives_considered: Continuous DRX (cDRX) which is common in high SFE materials, though the authors argue for a combination of dDRX and gDRX.
quotes: On the other hand, grains of hundreds of nm up to a few μm were observed at the grain boundary at 700 °C or higher, the temperature where yield strength drop occurred.
In other words, deformations at temperatures above 700 °C are expected to undergo both DRX and dynamic recovery (DRV) at the same time.

Compressive deformation microstructure observation confirmed that slip and DT were the dominant behaviors from room temperature to 600 °C, and slip and DRX were confirmed to be the major deformation mechanisms above 700 °C.

item.mechanism: Type-C serration at 600 °C is caused by cooperative lattice diffusion of constituent elements and interaction with nano-sized oxides, rather than interstitial solute atoms.
item.system: Equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi HEA additively manufactured by Selective Laser Melting (SLM)
item.operating_conditions: Compression at 600 °C with low strain rate
item.supporting_observation: Activation energy measured 335 kJ/mol, significantly higher than interstitial solute diffusion (76–103 kJ/mol) and similar to self-diffusion of constituent elements.
item.scope_limits: Does not apply to lower temperatures where serration is not observed; interstitial atoms are ruled out as the primary cause.
item.alternatives_considered: Interstitial solute atoms (C or N) causing aged dislocation unlocking; substitutional solute atoms alone.
quotes: Activation energy measured 335 kJ/mol, which was significantly higher than the activation energy related to the diffusion of common interstitial solutes (76–103 kJ/mol [67] ).
In other words, the serrated flow of SLM-built HEA can be uninfluenced by interstitial atoms, and this is related to the cooperative lattice diffusion of constituent elements.

In addition, the reason why the activation energy is higher than the self-diffusion activation energies of elements is suspected to be due to nano-sized Mn 2 O 3 , which can cause a serrated flow, also having an influence on deformation.

item.mechanism: Dynamic recrystallization proceeds via a combination of discontinuous DRX (dDRX) and geometric DRX (gDRX) rather than continuous DRX.
item.system: Equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi HEA additively manufactured by Selective Laser Melting (SLM)
item.supporting_observation: Flattened grains perpendicular to loading axis and grain boundary serrations observed; HR-EBSD shows ultra-fine grains formed by rotation of HABs rather than new strain-free grains.
item.scope_limits: Does not hold for materials with very low SFE where dDRX is the sole mechanism; cDRX is ruled out based on stress curve behavior.
item.alternatives_considered: Continuous DRX (cDRX) where saturation occurs; pure discontinuous DRX (dDRX) where flow stress decreases sharply.
quotes: Considering the characteristics described above, it is suspected to occur dDRX and gDRX during the high-temperature deformation of SLM-built HEA, simultaneously.
As seen in the curve, gDRX, where flow stress continuously decreases by small amounts, is somewhat different with dDRX, where flow stress decreases sharply, and cDRX, where saturation occurs.

In other words, the DRX of SLM-built HEA is caused by combination of dDRX and gDRX, which follow the process of i) accumulation of dislocations at HABs, ii) migration or bulging of HABs, and iii) rotation of HABs.

item.mechanism: Superior mechanical properties at high temperatures (up to 700 °C) are maintained because dislocation forest hardening and Orowan strengthening remain effective even when matrix and grain boundary strengthening diminish.
item.system: Equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi HEA additively manufactured by Selective Laser Melting (SLM)
item.supporting_observation: Yield strength decreases less significantly up to 700 °C compared to other temperatures; high dislocation density (1.88 × 10^14 m^-2) and fine precipitate spacing (82.07 nm) support this.
item.scope_limits: Does not hold above 700 °C where thermally activated mechanisms significantly reduce matrix and grain boundary contributions, though dislocation and Orowan effects persist.
item.alternatives_considered: Matrix hardening and grain boundary strengthening which decrease significantly at high temperatures.
quotes: Therefore, ∆ σ ρ and ∆ σ Or are expected to have an influence on the outstanding mechanical properties of SLM-built HEA, and this appears to be logical considering the dislocation density (1.88 × 10 14 m −2 ) and interparticle spacing between Mn 2 O 3 (82.07 nm) of the SLM-built HEA.

In high temperature conditions (above 700 °C), the outstanding high-temperature mechanical properties are achieved as σ ρ and σ Or have a significant influence on strengthening even though σ m and σ k cannot contribute due to the thermally activated mechanism.

The main reason why SLM-built HEA has outstanding mechanical properties is suspected to be due to the dislocation network, fine grain size and nano-sized Mn 2 O 3 that were observed in the initial microstructure.

item.mechanism: Epitaxial growth and specific texture development (<001>, <101>, <111>) result from heat dissipation direction during SLM, influencing mechanical properties.
item.system: Equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi HEA additively manufactured by Selective Laser Melting (SLM)
item.operating_conditions: As-built state; manufacturing process with specific scanning strategy
item.supporting_observation: Epitaxial growth grains observed in TD and SD planes; strong <001> texture along BD plus <101> and <111> textures detected; grain sizes vary by direction (5.98, 12.93, 15.66 μm).
item.scope_limits: Texture aspect can be changed by controlling scanning strategy; <101> texture is anticipated to improve strength and elongation compared to <001>.
item.alternatives_considered: Random texture or other texture types not observed in this specific SLM process.
quotes: The reason for this phenomenon is that the grains grow in the direction of heat release during AM, and thus it is considered that epitaxial growth appears as heat is released to BD in the TD and SD planes.
AM-processed steels [49] , [50] , Ni-based alloys [51] , [52] , Al-based alloys [53] , [54] and composites [55] , [56] are known to form a cellular or columnar structure within the grain.
It is commonly known that if an FCC alloy develops <101> texture, it will have a greater strength and elongation compared to <001> texture.
